# 1 Clement Chapter 26 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic Equivalence)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 26 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_026_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 26

**26:1** Is it really so hard to believe, then, that the Creator of all things will raise up those who have served him in holiness with sincere faith? After all, through a mere bird he already demonstrates the greatness of his promise!

**26:2** For scripture says somewhere: "You will raise me up and I will give you thanks;" and: "I lay down and slept; and then I arose, for you are with me."

**26:3** And Job himself says: "You will raise up this flesh of mine, which has endured all these things."

---

*PNEUMA brings out the rhetorical force of v. 1's a fortiori argument: if God does this through a bird, how much more will he do for his faithful servants.*
